ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scale-then-frame next-scale prediction for unified image and video generation
PROPOSAL: We extend Infinity-style bitwise next-scale prediction to video by treating each frame as a sequence of scales, ordering tokens scale-major within a frame and frame-major across time, so that an image is a one-frame video and the same model handles text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video by changing only the conditioning prefix. We train a 2B-parameter transformer on a mix of image-text pairs and 5-second clips at 480p, then adapt it to 720p with a short second stage.
CONTROLS: Baselines: a diffusion transformer of matched size trained on the same clips, an Emu3-style token-by-token raster model, and a frame-major variant that predicts all scales of frame t only after completing frame t-1. Ablations: scale-major against frame-major ordering, bitwise against index prediction, and the image share of the data mix at two levels.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Scale-major ordering within a frame should reach VBench scores within a few points of the diffusion baseline at under a tenth of its latency and beat the raster model on FVD on UCF-101. If motion smoothness lags far behind the diffusion model, the within-frame scale ordering is breaking temporal coupling and the frame-major variant should then win.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Obtaining a discrete video tokenizer by temporal expansion of an image tokenizer
PROPOSAL: We take the bitwise image tokenizer of Infinity, replace each 2D convolution by a causal 3D convolution whose central temporal slice carries the image weights and whose other slices start at zero, and fine-tune only the temporal slices and the quantizer on 17-frame clips at 256p before unfreezing everything briefly at 480p. The first frame is encoded exactly as an image would be, so images and videos share one codebook and one decoder.
CONTROLS: We compare against the same architecture trained from scratch on the same clips, against a tokenizer with the image weights copied into every temporal slice, and against the plain 2D tokenizer applied frame by frame. Reconstruction is measured by PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on UCF-101 and on a held-out web-video set, both at equal training steps and at the step where each tokenizer stops improving.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The expanded tokenizer should reach the rFVD of the from-scratch tokenizer in a small fraction of its training steps and keep image reconstruction unchanged. If the frame-by-frame 2D tokenizer matches it on rFVD, temporal compression is not what the generator needs from the tokenizer and the gain must come from the generator side.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coarse-scale history for long video generation with bounded context
PROPOSAL: We give the generator a context made of the last four frames at every scale plus only the two coarsest scales of all earlier frames, so that the attended sequence grows slowly while global layout and identity remain visible. Training randomises the cut-off so the model learns to work with any history length, and we optimise for the generation of two-minute videos at 480p in rounds of eight seconds, each conditioned on a new instruction.
CONTROLS: Full-history attention up to the length that fits, a pure sliding window of four frames without any coarse history, a window that keeps only the first frame as anchor, and a key-value cache compressed by token merging at equal memory. We measure subject consistency and background consistency on VBench-Long, drift of CLIP similarity to the first frame over time, and per-frame latency as the video lengthens, over three seeds.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Coarse-scale history should hold subject consistency within a few points of full attention while keeping per-frame latency flat, and beat the plain sliding window by a wide gap on background consistency. Failure would show up as the model ignoring the coarse history, in which case the first-frame anchor would match it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latency against quality at 720p for next-scale video prediction
PROPOSAL: We train a Visual AutoRegressive (VAR) style video generator with bitwise next-scale prediction, using a sixteen-frame latent clip at 720p and a schedule of ten scales per frame, and we measure the full trade-off between visual quality and wall-clock latency on a single accelerator. Quality is read from the Fréchet Video Distance (FVD) on Kinetics-600 and from the VBench benchmark suite, and latency is the time from prompt to decoded clip, including the tokeniser decoder.
CONTROLS: A Diffusion Transformer (DiT) baseline of matched parameter count at fifty, twenty and eight denoising steps, a next-token raster autoregressive model with key-value (KV) caching, and our model with fewer scales per frame. The Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) scale is tuned separately for each model on a held-out prompt set so that no method is compared at a setting chosen for another.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: At equal FVD the next-scale model should finish a clip several times faster than the diffusion baseline at its best step count, and at equal latency it should score higher on VBench than the eight-step diffusion model. If the gap closes at eight steps, the latency advantage is not large enough to matter at 720p.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-round instruction-following video extension in one discrete model
PROPOSAL: We train the unified next-scale generator with a conversational format in which each round appends a text instruction and a continuation of forty-eight frames conditioned on the whole previous video through compressed history. Training clips are cut into segments with per-segment captions produced by a captioning model, so that the generator sees instruction changes in the middle of a video. We evaluate five-round generations in which each instruction changes the camera motion or an object action.
CONTROLS: A single-round model asked to regenerate the whole video with the concatenated instructions, a diffusion extension baseline that continues from the last frames only, and our model with the history truncated to the current round. Metrics: per-round instruction adherence judged by a vision-language model and checked by two raters, subject consistency across rounds, and the share of rounds in which motion follows the new instruction.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: Round-by-round generation should follow new instructions in most rounds while keeping subject identity across rounds, and the diffusion extension baseline should drift on identity after the third round. The likely failure is that the generator ignores late instructions and continues the previous motion, which the adherence metric would show as a drop after round two.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Which temporal factorisation lets one next-scale model serve images and videos
PROPOSAL: We compare three ways of placing time inside next-scale prediction: spatiotemporal pyramids where each scale is a coarser video cube, per-frame scale pyramids ordered frame by frame, and per-frame pyramids predicting the residual against the previous frame at each scale. All three share the tokeniser, the 1B transformer and the data mix of images and clips, and all treat an image as a single-frame video.
CONTROLS: A text-to-image-only model of the same size as the upper reference for image quality, a video-only model as reference for FVD, and the raster next-token model as the autoregressive baseline. Ablations hold the number of scales fixed and vary only the ordering, and each configuration is run with three seeds on Kinetics-600 and on a text-to-image benchmark.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Per-frame pyramids with residual prediction should give the best motion smoothness at equal FVD, while spatiotemporal cubes should give the best image quality but the worst extrapolation. The whole comparison fails to inform if the three variants land within seed variance of one another.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bitwise vocabulary scaling for video tokens
PROPOSAL: We ask whether the bitwise prediction that lets Infinity grow its image vocabulary carries over to video tokens, where motion adds entropy. We train tokenisers with 16, 24 and 32 bits per token and generators that predict each bit with an independent sigmoid head, and we measure reconstruction and generation at 480p on Kinetics-600 and on a web-video corpus with captions.
CONTROLS: Index-prediction generators with a 2^16 codebook as the largest feasible softmax, a bitwise model with the same bit count but with bits predicted autoregressively within a token, and bit-flip corruption during training at three rates. We report rFVD of the tokeniser, FVD of generations and the gap between them, so that we can tell tokeniser limits from generator limits.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: We expect generation FVD to improve from 16 to 24 bits and to flatten at 32, with the gap to rFVD widening as bits grow. If the autoregressive-within-token variant beats independent bits by a wide gap, bit independence is the wrong assumption for motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-to-video and extrapolation as prefix conditioning
PROPOSAL: We test whether a next-scale video model trained only on text-to-video can perform image-to-video and video extrapolation by placing the tokens of the given image or clip in the context as already generated frames, with no new training, and then whether a short fine-tuning on mixed tasks closes any remaining gap. Evaluation uses the image-to-video track of VBench and an extrapolation protocol on UCF-101 where the model continues the first sixteen frames of each clip.
CONTROLS: A dedicated image-to-video diffusion baseline, the same next-scale model with task-specific fine-tuning, a variant in which the conditioning frames pass through the tokeniser with teacher-forcing noise, and a trivial baseline that repeats the last frame. Metrics include FVD of the continuation, first-frame fidelity, and identity drift measured by a face and object re-identification model.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Prefix conditioning without training should already give usable image-to-video with weaker motion than the fine-tuned variant, and extrapolation quality should fall slowly with the number of continued frames. If zero-shot extrapolation collapses after a few frames, the model has learned frames as position-bound rather than as a continuation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spatiotemporal attention patterns that keep long contexts affordable
PROPOSAL: We replace full attention in the video generator with structured patterns and measure quality against context length: within-frame full attention plus attention to the same spatial block in previous frames, attention to previous frames only at the coarsest scale, and a learned selection of the most relevant previous-frame tokens per query. Each model is trained from the same checkpoint on clips of sixty-four frames at 480p and evaluated on clips of twice the training length.
CONTROLS: Full attention trained on the same data as the quality reference, a plain sliding window as the cheap reference, and the sparse patterns without the coarse-scale link to separate the effect of sparsity from the effect of the link. We report FVD, temporal flicker, and the attention operations per generated frame.
COST: 1300
PREDICTION: The block-local pattern with a coarse-scale link should hold FVD within a few points of full attention at a fraction of its attention operations on long clips, and the learned selection should gain at longer lengths but lose at training length. Flicker rising sharply beyond training length would mean that none of the patterns generalises temporally.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-first curriculum for a unified discrete video generator
PROPOSAL: We train the next-scale model in three stages, images only, then clips of up to sixteen frames mixed with images, then clips of up to sixty-four frames, and compare against joint training on all data from the start, holding total tokens constant. We track text-to-image quality throughout to see whether video training erodes it, and we measure text-to-video quality on VBench at the end of each schedule.
CONTROLS: Joint training from the start, a curriculum without the image-only stage, and a curriculum with the image share held at half throughout. We also evaluate a model trained only on images and one trained only on clips as references. Three seeds per schedule on a 600M model before one run at 2B.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The staged curriculum should reach better text-to-video quality at equal tokens and keep image quality close to the image-only model. If joint training matches it, the curriculum is a convenience and not a necessity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Next-scale video generation with a bitwise tokenizer at 720p
PROPOSAL: Train one transformer that predicts video tokens scale by scale, where each scale covers a block of frames, so that text-to-image, text-to-video and image-to-video share one model and differ only in the number of frames. Initialize the discrete tokenizer from a pretrained image tokenizer and adapt it on 200000 clips for video reconstruction. Train the generator on WebVid-10M and a filtered LAION subset with recaptioned text, then evaluate 720p text-to-video on VBench and report wall-clock latency per clip on a single GPU type.
CONTROLS: Compare against Wan2.1 at the same output resolution and clip length, against an Emu3-style next-token model at the same parameter count, and against the same generator with a single frame per scale at matched training tokens. Report latency for each with the same batch settings, and repeat each generation with five random seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect VBench scores within about one point of the diffusion reference at several times lower latency per clip. The claim fails if the quality gap is wider than two points or if latency at 720p is not clearly better.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bitwise coarse-to-fine generation extended from images to short clips
PROPOSAL: Build a bitwise next-scale generator in the spirit of Infinity and extend its tokenizer to clips by stacking 8 frames along the channel axis before quantization. Pretrain on a filtered 50M LAION subset, fine-tune on 200000 WebVid-10M clips with captions rewritten by a vision-language captioner, and sample 720p outputs conditioned on earlier frames. Evaluate image quality on GenEval and video quality on VBench, and report wall-clock latency per sample on a single GPU type.
CONTROLS: Compare against Infinity at the same output resolution and image count, against a VAR-style class-conditional model at the same parameter count, and against the same generator with a single scale per image at matched training tokens. Report latency for each with the same batch settings, and repeat each generation with five random seeds.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect benchmark scores within about one point of the image reference at several times lower latency per sample. The claim fails if the quality gap is wider than two points or if latency at 720p is not clearly better.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initialization routes for a discrete video tokenizer
PROPOSAL: Compare three ways of obtaining a discrete video tokenizer: training from scratch, initializing from an image tokenizer, and initializing from an image tokenizer with a temporal-compression adapter inserted. Train each on the same 300000 clips of 33 frames at 256p, then measure reconstruction on MSRVTT and UCF-101 clips with PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS, and record the training hours needed to reach a target PSNR.
CONTROLS: Compare reconstruction across the three initializations with the same codebook and training clips, against a published continuous video autoencoder at the same compression ratio, with the optimizer momentum varied across its common range for each initialization, and with the evaluation clips drawn from the same domains and held fixed.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Initialization from the image tokenizer should reach the target reconstruction in a fraction of the training hours needed from scratch. If the adapter variant fails to improve PSNR over the plain initialization, the added temporal module is not justified.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bit width and loss weights in a discrete video tokenizer
PROPOSAL: Start from a discrete image tokenizer and study how the number of bits per token and the balance of reconstruction, perceptual and adversarial losses shape clip quality. Train variants on 300000 clips of 33 frames at 256p, using a common recipe, and report PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS on MSRVTT and UCF-101 together with the training hours consumed by each variant.
CONTROLS: Compare reconstruction across the three codebook bit widths with the same initialization and training clips, against a published image tokenizer applied frame by frame at the same compression ratio, with the optimizer momentum varied across its common range for each bit width, and with the evaluation clips drawn from the same domains and held fixed.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Higher bit widths should give better reconstruction at a modest cost in training hours. If the bit-width increase fails to improve PSNR over the narrowest width, the added codebook cost is not justified.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Block-summary attention for long multi-round video generation
PROPOSAL: Contain context cost by letting each new block of frames attend fully to the previous block and to a compressed summary of older blocks, built by pooling the coarse-scale tokens of each earlier block. Train on 10-second clips with captions that mix single and multiple instructions, then generate 30-second sequences under three successive text instructions. Score temporal consistency with the subject and background consistency dimensions of VBench and with a feature-drift measure between the first and last blocks.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention over the entire history on 30-second sequences, against a window of recent blocks without the summary on the same sequences, and against the same model with the summary pooled from the finest scales, reporting memory and throughput for each with matched batch settings.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect consistency scores close to the full-attention reference with memory growing slowly in sequence length. The claim fails if drift in the last block is clearly worse than the reference or if memory still grows quickly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Recent-frame window with a learned memory for video continuation
PROPOSAL: Cut attention cost with a sliding window over the most recent frames plus a small learned memory of coarse-scale tokens from earlier frames, updated after each block. Train on 10-second clips from a curated motion-rich set with captions that carry one instruction each, then examine the memory on continuations of real clips. Score temporal consistency with the subject and background consistency dimensions of VBench and with a feature-drift measure between the first and last blocks.
CONTROLS: Compare against full attention over the entire history on single-instruction sequences, against a window of recent blocks without the memory on the same sequences, and against the same model with the memory pooled from the finest scales, reporting memory and throughput for each with matched batch settings.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Expect consistency scores near the full-attention reference with memory growing slowly in sequence length. The claim fails if drift in the last block is clearly worse than the reference or if memory keeps growing quickly.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint image and clip training with motion-sensitive evaluation
PROPOSAL: Train one next-scale model on a mixture where 60 percent of samples are images and the rest are 49-frame clips, with the frame count signalled by the first scale. After training, evaluate image prompts on GenEval and clip prompts on VBench, reading motion quality from the dynamic degree, motion smoothness and temporal flickering dimensions, together with a small pairwise human preference study on motion for 200 prompts.
CONTROLS: Compare joint training against an image-only model on image fidelity measured with GenEval, against a video-only model on motion measured with dynamic degree and temporal flickering, and against the joint model on shuffled-frame clips to confirm that the motion scores react to frame order.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Joint training should keep image fidelity close to the image-only model while matching the video-only model on motion. The claim fails if either score drops clearly, or if motion scores stay unchanged on shuffled clips.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One next-scale model for stills and short clips judged by frame appearance
PROPOSAL: Fit a single next-scale model on a blend of still images and 49-frame clips, giving the frame count through a learned token at the start of the sequence, with 40 percent of the samples being images. Evaluate image prompts with Frechet inception distance on COCO and clip prompts with per-frame CLIP similarity and aesthetic scores, and add a small pairwise human preference study on frame appearance for 300 prompts.
CONTROLS: Compare joint training against an image-only model on image fidelity measured with Frechet inception distance, against a video-only model on appearance measured with per-frame CLIP similarity and aesthetic score, and against the joint model on shuffled-frame clips to confirm that the appearance scores react to frame order.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Joint training should keep image fidelity close to the image-only model while matching the video-only model on appearance. The claim fails if either score drops clearly, or if appearance scores stay unchanged on shuffled clips.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Next-scale video against diffusion and next-token references at 720p
PROPOSAL: Train a discrete next-scale video model with temporal blocks on 720p clips, using the video tokenizer initialized from an image tokenizer, and check that it reaches diffusion-level visual quality at much lower latency. Measure the VBench total score, a pairwise user study on 150 prompts, and end-to-end latency for 5-second clips, reporting each by task: text-to-video, image-to-video and extrapolation.
CONTROLS: Compare against Wan2.1 at 720p on the same GPU type with the same number of frames, against an Emu3-style next-token reference at matched visual quality, and against the same model with bidirectional attention inside each block, with latency reported for each over repeated runs.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Expect visual quality near the diffusion reference with latency several times lower. The claim fails if users prefer the diffusion output by a wide majority of votes or if the speed advantage vanishes once extrapolation is included.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scale-by-scale video generation tracked across training and decoding choices
PROPOSAL: Train a next-scale video model with temporal blocks on 720p clips, with a video tokenizer adapted from an image tokenizer, and chart how quality and speed change as training proceeds and as decoding is shortened. Measure the VBench total score, a pairwise user study on 150 prompts, and end-to-end latency for 5-second clips, reporting each by task: text-to-video, image-to-video and extrapolation.
CONTROLS: Compare against the checkpoints at 100000, 200000 and 300000 steps of the same model at 720p on the same GPU type with the same number of frames, against the same model decoded with fewer scales at matched visual quality, and against the same model with causal attention inside each block, with latency reported for each over repeated runs.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Expect visual quality to rise steadily over checkpoints with latency several times lower than the reference setup. The claim fails if later checkpoints stop improving by a wide majority of votes or if the speed advantage vanishes once extrapolation is included.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Placing time inside next-scale prediction: three factorisations compared
PROPOSAL: We compare three ways to put the temporal axis into coarse-to-fine prediction, spatiotemporal pyramids where each scale is a coarser video cube, per-frame pyramids ordered frame by frame, and per-frame pyramids that predict residuals against the previous frame, with one tokenizer, one 1B transformer and one data mix of images and clips in which an image is a single-frame video. We measure text-to-image quality, text-to-video quality and extrapolation from each factorisation.
CONTROLS: An image-only model of equal size as the image reference, with the published Infinity numbers on GenEval as a second point; a video-only model as the FVD reference; the raster next-token model as the autoregressive baseline; and three seeds per factorisation on Kinetics-600 and on GenEval.
COST: 1700
PREDICTION: Per-frame residual pyramids should win on motion smoothness and extrapolation while cubes win on image quality. If the three land within seed noise, the ordering does not matter and the tokenizer dominates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Keyframe synthesis with next-scale images plus learned interpolation
PROPOSAL: We generate videos by sampling keyframes every eighth frame with the Infinity image model conditioned on the text and on the previous keyframe tokens, then fill the gaps with a diffusion frame interpolator fine-tuned on Kinetics-600, so that the image model handles appearance and the interpolator handles motion. We measure text-to-video quality and extrapolation by chaining keyframes, and image quality on GenEval with the unchanged image model.
CONTROLS: Interpolation by optical-flow warping as the floor, a video diffusion model of equal size as the FVD reference, the keyframe model with and without the previous-keyframe conditioning, and three seeds for the interpolator on Kinetics-600.
COST: 1700
PREDICTION: Keyframe plus interpolation should reach competitive FVD on short clips with the image quality of the unchanged image model. The result would be refuted if large motions between keyframes make the interpolator blur, which flow warping would show first.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Discrete video tokenizers without training from scratch
PROPOSAL: We initialise a causal 3D tokenizer from a bitwise image tokenizer by placing the image weights in the centre temporal slice and zeros elsewhere, fine-tune the temporal slices and quantizer on seventeen-frame clips at 256p, then unfreeze briefly at 480p, and we track how many steps it takes to reach a target rFVD against training from scratch.
CONTROLS: The same architecture from scratch at equal steps and at convergence, the image weights copied into every slice, the frozen 2D tokenizer frame by frame as the floor, and MAGVIT-v2 at matched compression as an external point. We report PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on UCF-101 and generator FVD on codes from each tokenizer, with three seeds for the small generator and bootstrap intervals.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The expanded tokenizer should reach the target rFVD in a small fraction of the steps and give equal generator FVD. If equal rFVD still gives worse generator FVD, the codes differ in predictability rather than in fidelity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Higher-fidelity discrete video tokens through adversarial and perceptual losses
PROPOSAL: We train a causal 3D bitwise tokenizer from scratch on seventeen-frame clips at 256p and then 480p, adding a video discriminator, a perceptual loss from a frozen video encoder and a temporal flicker penalty, and we scale the training set from UCF-101 to a web corpus of millions of clips to see how far reconstruction quality rises.
CONTROLS: The same tokenizer trained with reconstruction loss only, the discriminator removed, the perceptual loss removed, the small and the large training sets, and MAGVIT-v2 at matched compression as an external comparison. We report PSNR, LPIPS and rFVD on UCF-101 and Kinetics-600, and generator FVD on codes from the best and the plain tokenizer, with three seeds for the small generator.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The adversarial and perceptual losses should lower rFVD by a wide gap and the larger corpus should lower it further. If generator FVD does not follow rFVD, higher-fidelity codes are harder to predict.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Compressing the spatiotemporal history that a video generator attends to
PROPOSAL: We keep the last four frames at full scale and all earlier frames only at their two coarsest scales, then train with random history cut-offs so the model tolerates any length, and we generate minute-long clips at 480p to measure how consistency and per-frame latency change as the history grows.
CONTROLS: Attention over the full history up to the longest length that fits, a four-frame sliding window, a first-frame anchor window as a check on identity alone, and key-value cache merging at equal memory, measured by VBench-Long consistency, FVD on UCF-101, CLIP drift to the first frame and per-frame latency, over three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Coarse history should hold consistency near full attention with flat latency, and beat the sliding window by a wide gap. If the first-frame anchor does as well, the model only needs identity, not layout history.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Speculative decoding with a small draft model for faster video token generation
PROPOSAL: We pair the next-scale video generator with a 300M draft model that proposes the bits of each scale, verified in one pass by the large model, and we measure the speed-up and any change in quality on minute-long clips at 480p, with both models attending to the complete history of generated frames.
CONTROLS: The large model decoding alone as the quality reference, the draft model alone as the floor, acceptance rates per scale, and two draft lengths with the acceptance threshold tuned on a held-out prompt set, measured by VBench-Long consistency, FVD on UCF-101 and per-frame latency, over three seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Speculative decoding should cut per-frame latency by about half at unchanged quality, with acceptance highest at coarse scales. If acceptance drops at the finest scales, the draft model is too small for texture detail and a larger draft should be tried.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One discrete model for image, video, image-to-video and extrapolation
PROPOSAL: We train a single next-scale transformer where an image is a one-frame video, and where the task is set only by the prefix: text alone for text-to-image and text-to-video, text plus the tokens of a given frame for image-to-video, and text plus the tokens of a given clip for extrapolation. Training samples the four prefixes from one captioned corpus, and we test each task against specialists of the same size.
CONTROLS: Four single-task models of equal size and data as specialists, the unified model with the image share removed, zero-shot image-to-video from the text-to-video-only model, and a diffusion baseline per task with its reported numbers checked on our prompts. Metrics are GenEval for images, VBench for video, first-frame fidelity for image-to-video and FVD of continuations for extrapolation, with three seeds.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: The unified model should match each specialist within a few points and beat the zero-shot variant on image-to-video by a wide gap. If the specialists win clearly on images, the mixed data hurts appearance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a video diffusion teacher into a next-scale discrete student
PROPOSAL: We raise the fidelity of a text-to-video next-scale transformer by distilling from a frozen video diffusion teacher: the student trains on teacher samples for the same captions and on a feature-matching loss between the student's last-layer activations and the teacher's denoiser features at the middle timestep, with the teacher's guidance scale fixed for all samples. We test whether the student reaches teacher-level quality while keeping the student's latency unchanged.
CONTROLS: The student trained on real clips only, the student on teacher samples without the feature loss, the teacher itself as the quality ceiling, and a raster autoregressive student distilled the same way, so that the gain is not specific to next-scale ordering. Metrics are VBench and FVD on UCF-101, plus latency per clip, with three seeds.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: Distillation should close most of the gap to the teacher on VBench at unchanged latency, with the feature loss adding a few points on top of sample distillation. If the real-clip student matches it, the teacher adds nothing beyond its captions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Extending generation across rounds of user instructions
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune the unified model on clips segmented into captioned parts so that each round adds an instruction and a continuation conditioned on compressed history, and we generate five-round videos where instructions change camera or object motion, then measure adherence per round and identity across rounds.
CONTROLS: One model given all instructions at once, a diffusion extension baseline that continues from the last frames, our model with history cut to the current round, and shuffled instructions as a check that text is read. Adherence is judged by a vision-language model and verified by two raters on 200 rounds, with subject consistency and FVD per round.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Round-wise generation should follow most instructions and keep identity where the diffusion extension drifts. If adherence falls after round three, the compressed history is swamping the new text.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text encoders and prompt adherence for single-clip discrete video generation
PROPOSAL: We train the next-scale video generator three times with different frozen text encoders, a T5-XXL encoder, a CLIP text encoder and the final layer of a decoder-only language model, on the same captioned corpus, and we measure how closely a single sixteen-frame clip follows prompts about camera motion and object actions, since adherence to instructions is what later rounds would build on.
CONTROLS: The three encoders at equal token length, a model with the text dropped at training time as the floor, a shuffled-caption check for the judge, and the adherence reported for Emu3 on the same prompts. Adherence is judged by a vision-language model and verified by two raters on 200 clips, with VBench and FVD.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The decoder-only encoder should give the best adherence on motion prompts and T5 the best on object prompts. If all three tie, the bottleneck is the tokenizer, not the text side.
